summary: Expose one fixed-endpoint MCP tool per FedEx operation plus a fixed set of local-data tools, and drop the generic endpoint executor and the raw CLI mirror.
reason: A shipping agent for a small business needs tracking, rates, labels, returns (call tags), pickups, end-of-day, open ship, and consolidations, but a generic endpoint selector and a CLI mirror that forwards raw arguments and global flags (--config, --deliver, --yes, file paths) cannot be constrained or reviewed per call.
validated_outcome: Tests pin the exact tool list; every endpoint tool's read-only annotation matches the client's read-only allowlist; write tools carry destructiveHint=true, idempotentHint=false, and an allow_duplicate override; no tool exposes args, config, deliver, yes, data-source, output, input, webhook, or endpoint_id; local tools accept only allowlisted command flags passed as --name=value with positionals after --; the companion CLI launched by MCP refuses every FedEx write; write results drop encoded labels and recipient fields but keep tracking numbers and net charges; shipments_create and ship_bulk save created shipments to the local archive without the raw response; MCP writes share a fixed pacer below FedEx's per-IP limit and ship_bulk stops sending when the call is canceled; local tools run the companion CLI with --json --no-input --no-color (not --agent, whose --compact would strip output); tools-manifest.json and mcp_tool_count match runtime registration.
